title: fix(app-shell): Studio holds a new dashboard widget unsent until it is bound, instead of drawing a red refusal (objectui#11910)
body:
Fixes #11910

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

On Studio's Interfaces page, *Add widget* on a dashboard in Design mode no longer draws a red refusal before the author can bind the widget. The new widget is held, as objectui#11786 holds an incomplete field or step on the Data and Automations pages: it stays on the canvas, unsaved, the widget inspector says what it needs, a neutral line names it, and Publish refuses while it is held. A save of a finished widget that is refused keeps objectui#11785's red strip.

- **The hold.** Before the leaf autosave of a dashboard sends, the pillar asks `dashboardHeldEdit` (new, in `metadataError.ts`) about the draft. It walks the widgets and, for each, asks the installed spec's own `DashboardWidgetSchema` (`widgetMissingInputs`). A widget is held when the spec refuses it and every issue it names is the absence of one of the inputs the widget inspector's dataset binding offers (Dataset, Dimensions, Values). The autosave is then `blocked`: the edit stays dirty and nothing is sent.
- **The line.** Where the leaf's refusal strip goes, `StudioHeldNotice` reads "Not saved yet: Dataset on the widget “New metric (kpi)” needs a value. Your changes are kept here and saved once it is filled in." It offers "Show me" when that widget's inspector is not the one open. Once a dataset is picked, the line names Values (measures). Picking a measure lets the next autosave go.
- **The inspector.** `DashboardWidgetInspector` shows the existing "Required. Changes are saved once this has a value." row under the Dataset picker, then under the measures editor, for exactly the inputs `widgetMissingInputs` returns.
- **Publish.** `InterfacesPillar` takes the optional `onHeldEditChange` the Data and Automations pillars already take, reports its held clause through `useHeldEditReport`, and the shell's mount passes `setHeldEdit`. While a widget is held, Publish shows "Not published: Dataset on the widget “New metric (kpi)” needs a value, so that change is not saved yet. Finish it, then publish." and publishes nothing.
- **Errors stay for finished work.** A widget the spec refuses for anything else is sent, and its refusal shows as before. That covers a value the author wrote wrong (a dataset name that is not an identifier, two measures on a metric), a type outside the spec's, and a missing key the inspector does not offer.

Nothing is added to the package entry: no export, prop, type member or language-pack key. `InterfacesPillar` and `metadataError.ts` do not reach `index.ts`. The one new string is a row of the metadata-admin designer's own table, `engine.studio.held.widgetNeedsInput`, in en and zh.

## Measured before acting (dispatch Zone 2)

- **H1, the pattern's parts.** Confirmed as the dispatch read them. `InterfacesPillar`'s leaf autosave was blocked only on `inspectorBlocking`, and its mount passed no `onHeldEditChange`. The new predicate joins the same `StudioHeld` shape.
- **H2, incomplete vs wrong, read off the spec.** Measured on the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 with `DashboardWidgetSchema.safeParse` on `{ id, type, title }`, as `handleAddWidget` builds it, for all 11 types `AddWidgetPicker` offers (`WIDGET_TYPE_META`). Every one is refused at exactly `dataset` and `values` (invalid_type, received undefined), and `DashboardSchema` on the whole dashboard names `widgets.N.dataset` and `widgets.N.values`, the card's live 422 paths. No picker type needs no binding, so the dispatch's control "a type that needs no binding saves at once" has no subject on 17.7.0. It is replaced by "an edit to a dashboard whose widgets are all bound saves at once". The reading is spec-derived: no list of required keys lives in objectui. The one local list is which inputs the inspector offers, so a widget is held only for an input the author can reach. My choice on the not-verified half: hold only when the spec's ONLY complaints are absences. A dataset name written wrong, with measures still absent, is sent and draws the strip (pinned). Held, it would show "needs measures", and a misnamed dataset offers none to pick. `values: []` is a value, not an absence, so it is not held (pinned as a boundary, see Acceptance notes).
- **H3, the target.** `{ kind: 'widget', id }`, as the canvas selects it. "Show me" reopens that widget's inspector after it was closed (pinned). The inspector did not mark Dataset or measures as required, so the hint was needed. `DashboardPreview.tsx` did not need to change.
- **H4, more than one buffer.** Only the leaf autosave is held. With a widget held, a nav entry added and bound in nav editing sends its app save while the dashboard stays unsent (pinned).
- **A live reading.** NOT MEASURED: no published 17.7.0 server is installed in this container. The spec parse above is the measurement, and its paths match the live 422 the card measured.

## Pins

- `metadataError.heldWidget-11910.test.ts` (the predicate). Every held case is paired with `DashboardSchema`'s verdict on the same dashboard, and every not-held control with a dashboard that judge accepts or refuses for something the author wrote. Covered: all 11 picker types held for Dataset; Dataset bound, held for Values; complete, not held and accepted; the first unfinished widget named; a map title read in the designer locale (zh), an untitled widget named by its id. Controls, not held: two measures on a metric, a dataset written wrong, `values: []`, a type outside the spec's, a widget with no id, and a dashboard with every widget bound or none.
- `InterfacesPillar.heldWidget-11910.test.tsx` (real `DashboardPreview` and `DashboardWidgetInspector`, a client double that records saves). *Add widget* → *Metric (KPI)*: no dashboard save after the debounce, no red strip, the line names Dataset, the inspector hint sits under Dataset, and the surface is told the clause. A dataset moves the line and the hint to Values. A measure sends one save, which `DashboardSchema` accepts, clears both, and reports `null`. "Show me" reopens the widget. Controls: a finished widget the server refuses shows the red strip and no held line; an edit to a dashboard whose widgets are all bound saves at once; a held widget does not hold the nav save.
- `StudioDesignSurface.heldWidgetPublish-11910.test.tsx` (the real surface on the real route). With a widget held, Publish refuses, naming it, and publishes nothing. Once it is bound and saved, Publish goes. With nothing held, Publish goes as before.

## Ablation (committed implementation, restore proven each leg)

Run through `ablation-replace` (anchor hit once, landed on disk, restored) under the shared verify lock, before the merge of `main`:

- **A**, the held predicate removed from the leaf autosave's `blocked`: `InterfacesPillar.heldWidget-11910` 3 failed of 6. First failure: "the unbound widget is not sent: expected [ { name: 'sales_dash', …(2) } ] to deeply equal []". The nav pin went red on its "the widget is still held" half. Show me, the refusal control and the all-bound control stayed green, as expected: they read the line or a finished widget.
- **B**, `widgetMissingInputs` told to skip a non-absence issue instead of answering none: `metadataError.heldWidget-11910` 2 failed of 10 (the wrong-dataset and off-type or no-id controls). "expected [ 'values' ] to deeply equal []".
- **C**, the `InterfacesPillar` mount's `onHeldEditChange` set to `undefined`: `StudioDesignSurface.heldWidgetPublish-11910` 1 failed of 3. "Publish must not go around the held widget: expected vi.fn() to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times". The first attempt at C was a no-op: its replacement text was contained in its anchor, the tool refused it ("the replacement count moved 1 -> 1"), and nothing ran. It was re-run with a replacement that lands.
- Each restore: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Tests and gates

Final head `53372bd` (this branch merged with `main` at `7241a81`, never rebased; the code is unchanged since `fd53a82`, which round 1 measured). Run from the worktree root:

- **Type-check** (locked), on `fd53a82`: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0. `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.ts(x)`, and its first run went red on the new publish pin's double signatures, which `fd53a82` fixes. Dependencies built with `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^... --concurrency=2`, 28 of 28 (all from turbo's cache), exit 0.
- **Tests** (locked), `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`, on `ed7dfa8`. `ed7dfa8` and `fd53a82` differ only in the publish pin's two type annotations.
  - `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` in full: 140 files, 892 tests passed, exit 0.
  - Every other app-shell and console test that imports `DashboardWidgetInspector`, `DashboardPreview`, `metadataError`, `StudioDesignSurface`, the inspector registration or the metadata-admin i18n table (derived by `git grep` on that head): 123 files, 1573 tests passed, exit 0.
  - The three new pins again on `fd53a82`: 3 files, 19 tests passed.
- **Declared narrowing:** app-shell's full suite is CI's. The derived set covers direct importers of the changed modules, and is blind to a test that reaches them only transitively.
- **ESLint** on the 7 changed source and test files: 0 errors and 24 warnings, every one on a line `main` already carries (same rules, the inspector's lines shifted by its one new import).
- **Gates**, all exit 0: control-bytes, test-path-roots, changeset-claims ("No pending changeset names a file this change touches."), pending-changeset-literals, i18n-keys, i18n-drift, i18n-dead-keys (the new row not reported), i18n-designer-parity ("Every en row has a zh row, and every shared row carries the same placeholders."), new-line-citations, spec-symbols, vi-mock-specifiers, vi-mock-inherit, vi-mock-override-shape, designer-field-key-parity, phantom-deps, metadata-write-doors, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, and `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` ("NOT GOVERNED").

## Eager closure (objectui#11937 is open on `main`)

`Bundle Analysis` is red on `main` itself, so it will be red here too. That is objectui#11937's work; nothing here touches the budget script or a ceiling. This change's own delta, measured by a local `vite build` of `apps/console` on both trees in this container (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144`, a full console build):

- base `f3a0488`: 3,386,819 bytes gzipped. `pnpm check:eager-closure` reads "3307.4 KB gzipped across 336 chunks, 0.4 KB over the 3307.0 KB budget".
- head (this branch's source): 3,387,202 bytes gzipped, "3307.8 KB … 0.8 KB over".
- Delta **+383 bytes gzipped** (+1,137 raw). Still 336 eager chunks of 2458. Per chunk: `src` +2,028 and `studioScope` −1,696, as `metadataError.ts`'s code follows the eager widget inspector that now imports it. `i18n` +41 for the two new rows. Five other chunks moved by 9 bytes or less.

Round 2: after main rolled back objectui#11931 and #11932 (objectui#11956) and raised the ceiling (objectui#11949), Bundle Analysis on `53372bd` passes: 3308.5 KB across 337 chunks, budget 3312.0 KB.

## Acceptance notes

- **File surface.** `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` carries two adjuncts beside its two named regions: the `dashboardHeldEdit` import, and the `onHeldEditChange` member of `InterfacesPillar`'s props, which the mount line needs. `DashboardPreview.tsx` is untouched.
- **The inspector's hint outside Studio.** `DashboardWidgetInspector` is also the registered inspector of metadata-admin's `ResourceEditPage`, whose own autosave does not apply this hold. There, "Changes are saved once this has a value" overstates what that page does. This is the same boundary `FlowNodeInspector`'s objectui#11786 hint already has.
- **Same family, not done here: an empty measure list.** Removing a widget's last measure writes `values: []`. The spec refuses that (`min(1)`), and this hold does not cover it, because it is a value and not an absence. The next autosave sends it and draws the red strip. It is reported to the seat for the family's closing card, not fixed here.
- **Reported, not fixed here: a stale refusal strip.** `InterfacesPillar`'s leaf `doSave` never clears `error` when a later save lands. The Data and Automations pillars clear it at the start of each save. After one refused dashboard save, the red strip stays on screen through every later successful save, until the leaf reloads. Measured with a one-off probe through the real pillar, which was not committed.
- **Prose only, not carded.** The `engine.inspector.widget.datasetHint` row still says the dataset "takes precedence over the inline object query above". That query was removed from the inspector at ADR-0021.
